candidates.title: AI-co-authored 'defensive publication' stakes prior art on a 2050 planetary concept
candidates.shift: A French-language open spec/reference implementation, explicitly co-written with multiple AI models, is filed as prior art to preempt future patent claims on an unnamed 'terrestrial ascension' concept.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative wild card: an odd emerging genre where humans plus AI models jointly publish speculative IP claims to stake ground in undefined future domains before anyone else can patent them.
candidates.evidence: Zenodo-hosted spec 'Ascension Terrestre 2050,' credited to ChatGPT o3, Claude Opus, Gemini 3, released under Apache 2.0 as a defensive prior-art publication.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of humans and AI jointly generating speculative 'prior art' documents to preemptively claim intellectual territory in undefined future domains. If this practice spreads, patent and IP systems may face a flood of AI-assisted speculative filings.
candidates.author: Xavier Pillet

candidates.title: A one-author 'doctrine' for AI-quantum-era maritime law
candidates.shift: A self-published legal treatise proposes an 'Algorithmic Liability Index,' fusing AI, quantum cryptography, and ecological collapse into a new maritime law doctrine.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative wild card: unlikely to be adopted, but flags a genre of solo 'doctrine' documents trying to seed future legal frameworks ahead of institutions via self-publication.
candidates.evidence: Zenodo treatise proposing a mathematical liability model ('AMLI') for maritime law addressing AI, quantum crypto, and ecological collapse.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of individuals attempting to author entire new legal doctrines outside institutional process, betting on future adoption. If any such 'doctrine' gained traction, it would signal a shift from state/treaty-driven maritime law to crowd-authored speculative legal frameworks.
candidates.author: mohamed kamal arafa el-rakhawi

candidates.title: Photo-elicitation reveals compressed generational identity in a tiny ethnic minority
candidates.shift: Three generations of the Oroqen, one of China's smallest ethnic minorities, construct identity through nostalgic photo narratives, revealing rapid 'generational compression' of cultural memory.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a proxy signal for accelerated language/culture death in ultra-small populations; the photo-elicitation method itself could be a reusable early-warning tool for other endangered cultures.
candidates.evidence: Peer-reviewed photo-elicitation nostalgia narrative study of three Oroqen generations, Frontiers in Psychology.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of ethnic identity shifting from lived continuity to mediated nostalgia within a single family across three generations. If this generational compression pattern generalizes, it suggests cultural transmission for very small populations is collapsing faster than language-death models assume.
candidates.author: Shan Cong

candidates.title: Mapping wild medicinal plants for cultivation before extinction
candidates.shift: Niche modelling is being used to identify both conservation and cultivation zones for overharvested medicinal plants (devil's claw) in southern Africa, pairing preservation with proactive domestication planning.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an early template for pre-emptive cultivation logistics applied to endangered wild-harvested species, adjacent to seed-bank/de-extinction style thinking but for plants still alive.
candidates.evidence: Comparative niche modelling study of two Harpagophytum species for conservation and cultivation opportunities, South African Journal of Botany.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from reactive conservation (protect what's left) to proactive domestication mapping (grow it deliberately) for wild medicinal species. If scaled, this logic could be applied broadly to other overharvested wild botanicals globally, shifting supply chains from wild-harvest to managed cultivation.
candidates.author: Anthony Mapaura, Tendai C Mhunduru

candidates.title: Call for a new global framework to protect endangered languages
candidates.shift: Linguists argue that existing international frameworks for language protection are structurally inadequate as language death accelerates, urging a new global protective mechanism.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a direct hit on language death as institutional failure; worth watching whether any actual policy body picks up this call, especially regarding minority and Celtic-language contexts.
candidates.evidence: Academic article by Ó Giollagáin and Ó Curnáin urging a new framework for global language diversity protection, discussed on r/linguistics with source article linked.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of academic reframing pushing language death from a passive cultural-loss narrative toward an active governance failure requiring new international mechanisms. If adopted, this could create binding protections akin to biodiversity treaties but for linguistic diversity.

candidates.title: Reminder that biology's biggest theories preceded their evidence
candidates.shift: An essay traces how major biological theories were formulated before direct experimental proof existed, reframing how paradigm-shifting theory actually emerges in science.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative meta-signal: useful epistemic frame suggesting future breakthrough theories (synthetic biology, fungal computing, astrobiology) may similarly outpace their evidence — relevant to how foresight itself should treat speculative science.
candidates.evidence: Asimov Press essay analyzing the origins of two major biological theories that predated experimental confirmation.
candidates.initial_analysis: A reframing of scientific progress from evidence-first to theory-first, which if taken seriously changes how funders and foresight practitioners should weight currently unprovable but structurally elegant hypotheses in emerging biology fields.
candidates.author: Asimov Press

candidates.title: AI as flawed mirror of selfhood
candidates.shift: An essay explores how AI reflects human self-image while missing something essential, framing a philosophical gap between AI-mediated reflection and authentic identity.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: soft cultural-anxiety signal about AI-mediated identity that could presage broader psychological or therapeutic discourse shifts as AI companionship/reflection tools proliferate.
candidates.evidence: Palladium magazine essay arguing AI offers reflection of the self but omits something vital from the picture.
candidates.initial_analysis: Part of a growing body of cultural commentary questioning whether AI's reflective capacities constitute genuine self-understanding or a hollow simulation, which could shape future norms around AI companionship and therapy tools.
candidates.author: Garrett W. Ennis

candidates.title: Culture-as-content erodes art's reality-illuminating function
candidates.shift: An essay argues the monetized attention economy and generative AI are collapsing the distinction between art and infinitely-scaled 'content,' undermining art's traditional social function.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: relevant to how craft/artisanal revival economics might position themselves against algorithmic content flood — a values-shift signal more than a technology signal.
candidates.evidence: MIT Press Reader essay on culture becoming 'content' under generative AI and attention monetization.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of cultural critique tracking a shift from art-as-meaning to art-as-content-volume, driven by generative AI and attention markets. If this framing spreads, expect backlash movements valorizing scarcity, provenance, and craft authenticity as counter-signals.
candidates.author: Paul Chan

candidates.title: 'Medical undercommons' framed as clinical response to mass incarceration
candidates.shift: A reconceptualization of prison health inequities calls for 'concrete utopian' liberation-medicine practice rather than incremental reform of carceral healthcare.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an unusually activist framing entering clinical psychiatry literature, potentially feeding into broader prison-design and decarceration discourse.
candidates.evidence: Culture, Medicine and Psychiatry article proposing a 'medical undercommons' framework as a response to US mass incarceration, engaging a 2025 special issue.
candidates.initial_analysis: Represents a shift from viewing carceral healthcare as a technical service gap to framing it as a site of political liberation practice. If this framing gains traction, expect more clinical literature adopting explicitly abolitionist or utopian language.
candidates.author: Philippe I. Bourgois

candidates.title: Jails become delivery points for peer-led addiction recovery
candidates.shift: Peer recovery support services are increasingly embedded directly inside jails as forensic/legal touchpoints, rather than only offered post-release.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: positions jails as recovery infrastructure nodes rather than pure custody sites, a carceral-technology-adjacent institutional shift that could scale as a decarceration-adjacent model.
candidates.evidence: Qualitative study of forensic peer recovery specialists identifying barriers/facilitators to jail-based peer recovery support implementation.
candidates.source: Journal of Community & Applied Social Psychology
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of carceral institutions repurposing custody time as a recovery-delivery window, shifting jails from purely punitive spaces toward hybrid care infrastructure. If scaled, this could reshape both jail design and post-release recovery ecosystems.
candidates.author: Spencer G. Lawson, Jennifer Pendleton, Evan Marie Lowder et al.

candidates.title: Citizen-gathered OSINT pushes into international courtroom evidence rules
candidates.shift: A normative gap is emerging as international courts (citing ICC case law) confront citizen-collected open-source digital evidence without clear admissibility standards.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: convergence of civilian OSINT culture with international criminal justice; could reshape evidentiary standards and incentivize crowdsourced atrocity documentation as formal legal practice.
candidates.evidence: Doctrinal legal analysis of Rome Statute provisions and ICC case law (Yekatom & Ngaïssona) on citizen-gathered OSINT admissibility.
candidates.source: Journal of Communication Sustainability and Empowerment
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from state/institutional monopoly on war-crimes evidence toward crowdsourced, citizen-verified digital documentation entering formal courts. If codified, this could professionalize a new global class of OSINT investigators feeding international justice systems.
candidates.author: Maria Florencia Carballo Nievas

candidates.title: Contesting whether 'ethical' social robots for autism are possible at all
candidates.shift: Academic debate is moving from 'how to design ethical AI social robots for autistic children' to questioning whether such robots can be ethical in principle.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: a second-order pushback against assistive-robotics hype, shifting the conversation from design guidelines to foundational legitimacy.
candidates.evidence: AI & Society paper interrogating the ethical viability of AI-driven social robots for autistic children amid intensifying academic debate.
candidates.initial_analysis: Represents a shift in assistive-technology ethics from incremental safety/trust frameworks toward foundational questioning of whether the entire category is ethically coherent. If this view spreads, it could slow deployment of social robots in vulnerable-population care.
candidates.author: Cansu Elmadagli

candidates.title: Outsourcing conservation law enforcement to residents
candidates.shift: A qualitative evaluation examines local community members taking on law-enforcement roles inside protected areas, blending civilian and state authority.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could be an early model for distributed, non-state enforcement structures relevant beyond conservation, e.g. climate-refugia policing or resource-scarcity zones.
candidates.evidence: Qualitative evaluation study of a community-based approach to protected area law enforcement, People and Nature journal.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of state enforcement functions being partially devolved to civilian communities in resource-constrained conservation contexts. If generalized, this model could inform hybrid civilian-state governance structures for other scarce or contested resources.
candidates.author: William Sharkey, Aidan M. Keane, Pablo Sinovas et al.

candidates.title: Ethiopia builds institutional readiness blueprint for drone disaster response
candidates.shift: A conceptual framework proposes a maturity model for UAV-based disaster risk management specific to Ethiopia's institutional context, ahead of actual widespread deployment.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative peripheral-geography signal: drone governance frameworks preceding infrastructure could indicate leapfrogging in disaster-response technology across the Horn of Africa.
candidates.evidence: Conceptual evidence-maturity and institutional readiness framework for UAV disaster risk management in Ethiopia, Research Square preprint.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from ad hoc disaster drone use toward institutionalized readiness frameworks in a lower-resource setting, potentially preceding equivalent frameworks in wealthier nations. If adopted, this could become an exportable governance template for drone disaster response elsewhere in the Global South.
candidates.author: Mekibib Fisiha Tesfamariam

candidates.title: Recalibrating habitability beyond Earth-twin bias
candidates.shift: Astrobiology modeling is expanding habitability assessments to include Venus-like terrestrial worlds, shifting focus away from pure Earth-clone search criteria.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could reshape target-selection logic for future biosignature missions and reframe 'habitable' to include transiently or partially habitable planetary states.
candidates.evidence: Peer-reviewed application study modeling Venus-analog terrestrial planets for habitability, Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy.
candidates.initial_analysis: Represents a conceptual widening of 'habitable' beyond Earth-analog criteria to include hostile-seeming worlds, which could redirect future telescope time and mission targeting priorities. Over decades this reframing could change public and scientific expectations about where life might be found.
candidates.author: Swathi Raviprakash, Madhu Kashyap Jagadeesh, Margarita Safonova et al.

candidates.title: Machine-to-machine diplomacy needs its own security doctrine
candidates.shift: Multiple competing AI-agent communication protocols (MCP, A2A, Agora, ANP) are prompting cross-protocol security threat modeling before any single standard dominates.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative early indicator of an emerging 'internet of agents' needing governance akin to early internet protocol wars; could presage new cyber-conflict surfaces between autonomous agents.
candidates.evidence: Comparative academic threat-modeling paper analyzing security risks across four competing AI-agent communication protocols.
candidates.source: Journal of Information Security and Applications
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of infrastructure governance racing to catch up with a proliferating, uncoordinated set of machine-communication standards, echoing early internet protocol fragmentation. If unresolved, this could create persistent security seams between AI agent ecosystems.
candidates.author: Zeynab Anbiaee, Mahdi Rabbani, Mansur Mirani et al.

candidates.title: ML tools target copy-move forgery obscured by geometric transforms
candidates.shift: Forensic image-authentication research is advancing to catch geometrically transformed (rotated, scaled) copy-move forgeries that were previously harder to detect.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: incremental technical advance relevant to both art-forgery detection and deepfake/documentary evidence integrity, as forgery sophistication rises alongside detection tools.
candidates.evidence: Machine-learning method study for detecting geometrically transformed copy-move color image forgery, African Journal of Applied Research.
candidates.initial_analysis: Part of the ongoing arms race between digital forgery techniques and detection algorithms, extending from simple copy-paste manipulation to geometrically disguised forgeries. As forgery sophistication rises, this cat-and-mouse dynamic could extend to authentication of AI-generated imagery in legal and art-market contexts.
candidates.author: M. Talib Mahdi, W. Zaki Mizyad Al – Humadi, B. Arif Salim et al.

candidates.title: Post-quantum governance still stuck in review-paper stage
candidates.shift: Literature indicates cryptographic security policy for quantum computing remains largely at the systematic-review stage, with governance practice lagging behind technical PQC standards.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence signal: the lack of enacted policy frameworks despite finalized technical PQC standards suggests governance, not technology, is the real bottleneck to quantum-safe transition.
candidates.evidence: PRISMA-guided systematic literature review on quantum computing security policies, Discover Computing.
candidates.initial_analysis: Illustrates a widening gap between technical readiness (finalized PQC algorithms) and institutional/regulatory readiness (governance frameworks), a classic pattern where policy structurally lags fast-moving technical standards. If unresolved, organizations may face a 'quantum harvest now, decrypt later' exposure window.
candidates.author: Josué Naranjo Cordero, Sergio Mauricio Martínez Monterrubio, G. Torralba Elipe

candidates.title: Post-quantum migration splits into two incompatible tracks
candidates.shift: Organizations are discovering that IT and OT (operational technology) require separate post-quantum cryptography migration strategies rather than a single unified program.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative second-order implication of PQC standardization: industrial control systems may lag consumer IT migration, creating new attack-surface asymmetries between sectors.
candidates.evidence: Comparative risk analysis of post-quantum cryptographic adoption across IT and OT environments, referencing NIST PQC standardization.
candidates.initial_analysis: Represents a bifurcation of a technology transition once assumed unified, exposing industrial/critical infrastructure systems to a longer vulnerability window than consumer IT. If OT lags significantly, expect targeted attacks exploiting the migration gap in coming years.
candidates.author: Simon Baradziej

candidates.title: Orbital land-rush outpaces space law
candidates.shift: Rapid deployment of LEO mega-constellations (Starlink, OneWeb, Amazon LEO) is outstripping the 1967-era international space law framework meant to govern orbital use.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative trend flag for orbital mechanics/space law fringe: expect follow-on debates over debris liability, orbital slot 'ownership,' and eventual salvage/mining claim precedents.
candidates.evidence: Legal analysis of regulatory challenges from satellite mega-constellation proliferation under existing international space law, University of Leeds/Sheffield/York.
candidates.initial_analysis: A well-documented trend of private orbital deployment scale outpacing 1960s-era treaty frameworks, driving toward eventual crisis points around debris liability and orbital slot allocation. If unresolved, expect ad hoc national or corporate claims to fill the legal vacuum, echoing historical maritime flag-of-convenience dynamics.
candidates.author: Rohit Jayade

candidates.title: Blockchain drug-traceability model, still theoretical
candidates.shift: Another blockchain-based pharmaceutical supply-chain traceability proposal, following a long-running genre of blockchain-solves-supply-chain papers with limited real deployment.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative hype label: pattern-matches years of blockchain-supply-chain proposals; worth tracking only if it moves from proposal to real pilot deployment.
candidates.evidence: Peer-reviewed proposal for a scalable, transparent blockchain-based pharmaceutical supply chain drug-traceability model.
candidates.initial_analysis: Represents the continuation of a long-standing hype cycle around blockchain for supply-chain transparency, with limited historical real-world adoption. Included as a rule-out/context item rather than a genuine emerging signal.
candidates.author: Md Nurul Hasan, Sagnik Datta, Suyel Namasudra
